design.text: Randomized, double-blind, noninferiority trial comparing IV plazomicin to IV meropenem, with an option to switch to oral therapy after at least 4-5 days of IV treatment.

citations.quote: Study ACHN-490-009 (Study 009) was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, NI trial, in which patients \ge 18 years of age with cUTI, including acute pyelonephritis, were randomized to IV plazomicin (15 mg/kg/day) or IV meropenem (1.0 g every 8 hours).

The Applicant conducted one double-blind noninferiority (NI) Phase 3 trial in adults with cUTI, including acute pyelonephritis where plazomicin was compared to meropenem with an option to switch to oral therapy after at least 5 days of intravenous (IV) treatment.

population.text: Adults >=18 years with complicated urinary tract infection, including acute pyelonephritis; mMITT median age 64 years, 52.8% female, 99.5% White, with about 41.8% having pyelonephritis.

citations.quote: The mMITT population consisted of 388 patients with cUTI, including 162 (41.8%) with pyelonephritis. The median age was 64 years, 52.8% were female and 99.5% were White.

endpoint.text: Co-primary endpoint of composite cure (clinical success and microbiologic eradication) in the mMITT population at the Day 5 and Test-of-Cure (TOC) visits.

citations.quote: The co-primary endpoints were a composite of microbiologic eradication and clinical cure rate in the microbiologic modified intent-to-treat (mMITT) population at the Day 5 and TOC visits.

n.text: 609 patients randomized; mMITT population 388 (191 plazomicin, 197 meropenem)

citations.quote: A total of 609 patients were randomized; the mMITT population included 388 patients, 191 in the plazomicin arm and 197 in the meropenem arm.

result.text: At Day 5, composite cure 88% (168/191) plazomicin vs 91.4% (180/197) meropenem, difference -3.4 (95% CI -10.0, 3.1); at TOC, 81.7% (156/191) plazomicin vs 70.1% (138/197) meropenem, difference 11.6 (95% CI 2.7, 20.3); plazomicin was noninferior within the prespecified -15% margin.

citations.quote: At Day 5, composite cure rates in the plazomicin arm were 88% (168/191) and 91.4% (180/197) in the meropenem arm, treatment difference of -3.4 (95 % confidence intervals (CI), -10.0, 3.1). At the TOC visit, composite cure rates in the plazomicin arm were 81.7% (156/191) and 70.1% (138/197) in the meropenem arm, treatment difference of 11.6 (95 % CI, 2.7, 20.3).
The lower bound of the 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the composite endpoint of clinical response and microbiologic eradication were within the pre-specified NI margin of -15% at both visits.

indication.text: ZEMDRI is an aminoglycoside antibacterial indicated in patients 18 years of age or older for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae.

citations.quote: ZEMDRI is an aminoglycoside antibacterial indicated for the treatment of patients 18 years of age or older with Complicated Urinary Tract Infections (cUTI) including Pyelonephritis. (1.1)

ZEMDRI is indicated in patients 18 years of age or older for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis caused by the following susceptible microorganism(s): *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Proteus mirabilis*, and *Enterobacter cloacae*.

target_moa.text: Plazomicin is an aminoglycoside (derived from sisomicin) that binds to the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, thereby inhibiting protein synthesis and exerting concentration-dependent bactericidal activity; it retains activity in the presence of many aminoglycoside modifying enzymes.

citations.quote: Plazomicin is an aminoglycoside that acts by binding to bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, thereby inhibiting protein synthesis. Plazomicin has concentration-dependent bactericidal activity as measured by time kill studies.
Plazomicin is an aminoglycoside antibacterial drug derived from sisomicin. Plazomicin has activity in the presence of some aminoglycoside modifying enzymes (AMEs).
Plazomicin (ZEMDRI) for injection is an aminoglycoside antibacterial drug.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=1%) are decreased renal function, diarrhea, hypertension, headache, nausea, vomiting and hypotension. In Trial 1, adverse reactions associated with renal function occurred in 3.6% (11/303) of ZEMDRI patients vs 1.3% (4/301) meropenem, and serum creatinine increases >=0.5 mg/dL occurred in 7% (21/300) vs 4% (12/297).

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (\ge 1% of patients treated with ZEMDRI) are decreased renal function, diarrhea, hypertension, headache, nausea, vomiting and hypotension. (6.1)

In Trial 1, the incidence of adverse reactions associated with renal function (acute kidney injury, serum creatinine increased, chronic kidney disease, creatinine clearance decreased, renal failure, renal impairment) was 3.6% (11/303) in ZEMDRI-treated patients compared with 1.3% (4/301) in meropenem-treated patients [see *Adverse Reactions (6.1)*].
Serum creatinine increases of 0.5 mg/dL or greater above baseline occurred in 7% (21/300) of ZEMDRI-treated patients compared with 4% (12/297) of meropenem-treated patients.

detail.text: Boxed warning for NEPHROTOXICITY, OTOTOXICITY, NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCKADE and FETAL HARM: nephrotoxicity (greater risk in renal impairment, elderly, concomitant nephrotoxic drugs); ototoxicity (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, possibly irreversible); neuromuscular blockade; and fetal harm in pregnant women.

citations.quote:
## **WARNING: NEPHROTOXICITY, OTOTOXICITY, NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCKADE and FETAL HARM**
## *See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning.*

- Nephrotoxicity has been reported with ZEMDRI. The risk of nephrotoxicity is greater in patients with impaired renal function, the elderly, and in those receiving concomitant nephrotoxic medications. (5.1)
- Ototoxicity, manifested as hearing loss, tinnitus, and/or vertigo, has been reported with ZEMDRI. Symptoms of aminoglycoside associated ototoxicity may be irreversible and may not become evident until after completion of therapy. (5.2)
- Aminoglycosides have been associated with neuromuscular blockade. During therapy with ZEMDRI, monitor for adverse reactions associated with neuromuscular blockade particularly in high-risk patients. (5.3)
- Aminoglycosides, including ZEMDRI can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. (5.6, 8.1)
